html:
The Paramaras ruled Malwa in central India from about the 10th century until 1305, with their capital at Dhara.

They began as vassals of the Rashtrakutas and became independent under Siyaka. Their most famous king, Bhoja, ruled in the early 11th century. He was remembered as the ideal scholar king, credited with books on poetry, architecture and medicine, and with the great Shiva temple at Bhojpur; see the Bhojeshwar Temple.

The Paramaras were rarely at peace. They fought the Western Chalukyas in the Deccan, the Solankis of Gujarat and the Chandelas, and by the 12th century they were much weakened. In 1305 the armies of Alauddin Khalji conquered Malwa for the Delhi Sultanate.
sum: The Paramaras ruled Malwa in central India from about the 10th century until 1305, with their capital at Dhara.
